newsitem.title: USA: Carolina Harris nuke seen restarting Fri.
newsitem.headline: Carolina Harris nuke seen restarting Fri.

text.p: Carolina Power and Light Co's 880 megawatt Harris nuclear power plant in New Hill, N.C. is expected to resume electricity production September 6 after tripping off line earlier this week, a spokeswoman said.
"Our plan now is to resume operations early tomorrow afternoon," company spokeswoman Michele Warren said Thursday.
However, restart of the unit may have to be postponed depending on the effects of Hurricane Fran, Warren said.
"If we were to get the extremely high winds we would have to postpone the restart, but right now we are not expecting those high winds," she said.
New Hill is about 22 miles southwest of Raleigh, in the middle of North Carolina.
Hurricane Fran was expected to hit the U.S. coast near the border of North and South Carolina late Thursday.
Carolina Power has already shut its Brunswick nuclear power facility in anticipation of Hurricane Fran. The Brunswick plant is at Southport, N.C., on the coast and close to the forecast path of Fran.
The Harris unit was manually tripped off line late Tuesday after the failure of a service water pump.
Warren said repairs could also be delayed by a tornado watch in the area, as workers used a crane Thursday to replace a pump valve.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
